subject: Re: SOC2 / SIG evidence request — session traces & tenant parity
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aureliatherapeutics.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: Tim Rhodes <tim.rhodes@aureliatherapeutics.com>, AuditPartner <attn-compliance@auditsolutions.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence — session traces & tenant parity

Hi Kimberly,

Hope you’re well. We’re assembling Redwood’s SIG and CAIQ evidence for our internal SOC 2 scoping and have a couple of focused questions about data retention and deletion for tenant-scoped inference artifacts. Specifically: 

1) Session traces / inference request logs: can you confirm the default retention window for session traces in the eu region and whether there is any per-tenant variance option? We need explicit language we can include in our control mappings.

2) KV cache / in-memory model artifacts: does Redwood ever persist tenant-specific KV cache or model-serving state to durable storage (S3/equivalent)? If yes, under what conditions and retention window? If no, can you provide an auditable statement we can reference in the SIG worksheet?

3) For customers requesting targeted deletion (proof-of-delete), what deliverables do you provide? We’d like an example deletion manifest for one tenant (fields such as object id, deletion timestamp, checksum) and a short description of the verification process.

We’d appreciate a consolidated SOC2/SIG bundle (CAIQ mapping + sample deletion manifest + any attestations) by Friday 23 July to stay on schedule. If there’s any technical nuance we should call out in the CAIQ (e.g., debug snapshots vs. production traces), please flag it.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30-min call if that helps.

Best,
Lara Chen
Senior Security Operations
Aurelia Therapeutics

Attachments: SOC2-ask-outline.pdf (pdf)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aureliatherapeutics.com>
Cc: Tim Rhodes <tim.rhodes@aureliatherapeutics.com>, AuditPartner <attn-compliance@auditsolutions.io>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence — session traces & tenant parity

Lara,

Thanks for the clear ask and timeline — we can produce the bundle by 2027-07-23. Quick clarifying Qs so we give exactly what you need:

- Granularity: are you asking for per-request logs (every token/request metadata) or higher-level session traces (session id, start/end, outcome)?
- Proof-of-delete: do you want a one-off example for a non-production tenant we create for you, or an example manifest from our internal test tenant (redacted)?
- Regulatory scope: you noted Aurelia is EU-based — confirm if you need GDPR-specific language or only SOC 2 / SIG mapping.

I’m looping in Jonas Weber (Security) and Marissa Cole (R&D compliance lead) to scope the technical artifact set. Ben Carter (your AE) is CC’d for any contract or logistics that might impact delivery.

Plan: Jonas/Marissa will draft the attestation language for KV cache and session traces, I’ll assemble the CAIQ mapping, and we’ll attach a sample deletion manifest. If that timeline works, we’ll send the bundle and a short cover note on 23 Jul.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Sales Operations Manager
Redwood Inference

--
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference platform

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2027 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence — session traces & tenant parity

Jonas / Marissa — forwarding Aurelia’s ask (see below). Target drop: 2027-07-23. Can you:

- Draft a short attestation paragraph we can include in the SIG sheet that states our retention and deletion posture for (a) session traces and (b) KV cache / model-serving state;
- Produce a sample deletion manifest (CSV) structure we can populate and attach;
- Confirm whether there are any region-specific differences for eu vs us that we must call out in CAIQ cells.

Technical notes from infra (please refine):
- KV cache: purely in-memory on the inference host. Not persisted to durable object stores during normal serving. There are ephemeral debug snapshots created during failures; those snapshots (when captured) are retained for 14 days by default and stored in region-locally encrypted storage for debugging (rotated per KMS policy).
- Session traces: we persist aggregated request traces (request id, session id, timestamps, model version, route) for 30 days by default in eu regions for monitoring and billing; full per-token payload is not kept unless debug mode is enabled and a sampling policy captured the request.

Jonas — can you confirm the wording above and propose the final attestation? Marissa — can you produce a redacted sample-delete CSV with these columns: object_id, tenant_id, artifact_type, deletion_timestamp_utc, deleted_by, verification_hash? Ben — flag any contractual asks (SLA/AAAs) that would affect the wording.

Thanks,
Kim

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@aureliatherapeutics.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, AuditPartner <attn-compliance@auditsolutions.io>
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SOC2/SIG evidence — session traces & tenant parity

Hi Lara / team — attaching the requested bundle and a short summary below. Deliverables are attached as: SIG-evidence-bundle-20270723.zip (contains CAIQ mapping tab called "Aurelia - session & KV mapping" and a redacted sample deletion manifest).

Summary (short):
- KV cache / model-serving state: Redwood does not persist tenant-scoped KV cache to durable object stores during normal inference. KV cache is maintained in-memory on inference nodes and purged on instance shutdown or after cache eviction policies. Exception: ephemeral debug snapshots captured during incident investigation may be written to encrypted region-local storage for up to 14 days and are strictly access-controlled.

- Session traces / request logs: Aggregated request traces (request_id, session_id, timestamps, route, model_version, token_count) are retained for 30 days in EU regions by default for monitoring, billing, and quality checks. Full request payloads (message contents / per-token text) are not persisted unless debug capture is enabled by the customer and sampled per our capture policy.

- Proof-of-delete & manifest: Attached sample-delete-manifest-aurelia.csv demonstrates the manifest fields we provide for targeted deletion requests (object_id, tenant_id, artifact_type, deletion_timestamp_utc, deleted_by, verification_hash). For customer-triggered deletions we supply the manifest and a system audit id; we can also provide a signed deletion attestation on request.

What we included in SIG/CAIQ: the CAIQ mapping spreadsheet maps the control IDs you referenced to our technical design and the specific retention windows above (see the CAIQ tab). If you want, we can supply a short redlined control narrative for your SOC 2 auditor.

Next steps: I can join a 30-min call next week to walk through the bundle and answer auditor questions. Proposed slots: Mon 26 Jul (10–11 PDT) or Tue 27 Jul (14–15 PDT).

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Head of Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: SIG-evidence-bundle-20270723.zip (contains CAIQ-mapping-sheet.xlsx, sample-delete-manifest-aurelia.csv)
